surfaceForm: The mapping above is built primarily against EU instruments because they are the institution's own binding context.
location: ch33-regulatory-mapping-EN.tex :: \section{Applicability beyond the EU jurisdiction} (sec:rm-beyond-eu, line ~578)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the assertion that EU law is 'the institution's own binding context' with a role-based framing: 'the regulatory regime of the institution's home jurisdiction'. The chapter should not presuppose that the adopting institution is EU-based; the EU mapping should be presented as the worked instantiation, not as the reader's own context.
rationale: States that EU instruments are the reader's binding context, which is true only for an EU-based institution (University of Luxembourg). For an institution-agnostic Reference this is an implicit national/regional binding-context assumption stated without naming the home country.

surfaceForm: Whole chapter structure: primary mapping built against EU instruments (GDPR, NIS2, AI Act, Schrems II, eIDAS 2) with non-EU treated as 'substitution' / 'functional analogue' in sec:rm-beyond-eu
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the EU instruments as the primary worked example (they are well-documented and the international audience encounters them), but reframe the chapter introduction so the EU mapping is explicitly one parameterised instantiation of a jurisdiction-neutral spine (ISO/COBIT/NIST), rather than the default to which other jurisdictions are 'substitutes'. The role-based decision is: lead with the jurisdiction-neutral frameworks, then present EU as the reference instantiation.
rationale: The document's default-EU-then-substitute structure encodes an implicit home-jurisdiction (EU) bias. sec:rm-beyond-eu already provides the generic spine; promoting it from an appendix-style afterthought to the primary frame would make the chapter institution- and jurisdiction-agnostic by design rather than by caveat.

surfaceForm: The phase-2 international university network is the natural locus for sharing transposition notes and harmonising the practical interpretation of the framework above.
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the suite-specific 'phase-2 international university network' roadmap reference with a role-based construct, e.g. 'a peer network or community of practice among adopting institutions'. The mechanism (shared transposition notes) is generic; the named phase-2 programme is specific to this Reference's own deployment roadmap.
rationale: 'phase-2 international university network' is an artefact of this particular Reference's multi-phase rollout plan, not a property of any adopting institution. It assumes the reader is participating in this specific programme, which breaks institution-agnosticism.

surfaceForm: research-intensive university (recurring, e.g. 'most likely to apply to a research-intensive university', 'the research-intensive university context')
location: ch33-regulatory-mapping-EN.tex :: caveatbox (line ~32), sec:rm-method (line ~61), sec:rm-ai-act caption (line ~253), sec:rm-eidas2 (lines ~393, ~405)
proposedGenericDecision: Decide whether the Reference's target institutional role is exactly 'research-intensive university' or the broader 'research-and-education institution / higher-education institution'. If the suite targets a broader set of adopters, parameterise the institution-type noun phrase; if 'research-intensive university' is the intended fixed role, keep but record it as a named design constant.
rationale: The institution type is a fixed role assumption woven through the prose. It is not UL-specific by name, but it constrains the adopter profile; for an institution-agnostic matrix it should be an explicit parameter (some adopters are teaching-focused universities, research institutes, or university hospitals).

surfaceForm: sovereignty-grid review by the management body; cross-cutting management body cadence; 'the management body' (NIS2 Art.20, COBIT EDM01)
location: ch33-regulatory-mapping-EN.tex :: sec:rm-nis2 table Art.20 (line ~189), sec:rm-cobit table EDM01 (line ~534)
proposedGenericDecision: 'Management body' is drawn from NIS2 terminology and is acceptably generic, but verify it does not implicitly map onto a specific UL governance organ (rectorate / board of governors). Keep the regulation-sourced term 'management body' and avoid binding it to any one institutional organ; ensure no UL-specific governance-organ name leaks in cross-referenced chapters.
rationale: 'Management body' is the NIS2 Art.20 statutory term and is jurisdiction-neutral; no rectorate/board-of-governors language appears in this file. Flagged only as a governance-shape touchpoint to verify the cross-referenced layer/wave chapters do not concretise it to a UL organ.

surfaceForm: the institution's AI governance body; the institution's CIO office
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as role-based descriptors ('AI governance body', 'CIO office') which are already generic functional roles rather than named UL organs. No change needed beyond confirming the institution instantiates them under its own governance shape.
rationale: Both are generic functional-role references, not UL-specific organ names; they presuppose such functions exist but that is a reasonable institution-agnostic assumption. Recorded for completeness of the governance-shape scan.

surfaceForm: integration with REN-ISAC / sectoral feeds (A.5.7 Threat intelligence)
proposedGenericDecision: REN-ISAC is a North-American research-and-education ISAC; pairing it as the example threat-intel feed implicitly assumes a particular regional sector membership. Generalise to a role-based descriptor: 'a research-and-education sector threat-intelligence sharing community (e.g. an R&E ISAC)'.
rationale: REN-ISAC is a specific named sectoral body tied to a particular region's R&E community. Naming it as the integration target presupposes membership in that specific community, which a non-member institution would not have; it should be a parameterised role-based example.

surfaceForm: Identity-federation pattern (eduGAIN, eduTEAMS); SAML2 / OIDC carriage
proposedGenericDecision: eduGAIN and eduTEAMS are specific GEANT-operated R&E federation services. They are reasonable sector-standard examples but presuppose participation in the GEANT/inter-federation ecosystem. Keep as illustrative named instantiations but mark them as examples ('e.g. eduGAIN/eduTEAMS') so a non-participating institution substitutes its own federation; the generic role is 'inter-institutional identity federation'.
rationale: eduGAIN/eduTEAMS are named region/sector-specific services (GEANT ecosystem). The architectural role (notified-eID-scheme-compatible federation) is generic; the named services are a localisable instantiation, not universal.

surfaceForm: Network-layer zone-based segmentation; Cilium / Open vSwitch instantiation; SLSA / Sigstore supply-chain pattern; identity-layer MFA / FIDO2 baseline; OIDC / SAML2
location: ch33-regulatory-mapping-EN.tex :: sec:rm-iso table (A.8.22 line ~482, A.8.30 line ~488, A.8.5 line ~473), sec:rm-nis2 (lines ~201, ~210)
proposedGenericDecision: These are technology-product instantiations (Cilium, Open vSwitch, SLSA, Sigstore, FIDO2) not jurisdiction-specific, so they are NOT institution-specificity blockers. The Reference's own convention is to name reference instantiations as replaceable examples. No generalisation needed for institution-agnosticism; keep.
rationale: These are vendor/protocol instantiations, not institutional or jurisdictional specificity. They do not bind the document to University of Luxembourg or any single institution/jurisdiction, so they fall outside the detection scope; recorded as explicitly-cleared to document the scan.

surfaceForm: Member States vary in the sectoral scope of NIS2 ...; Several Member States have adopted national data-protection acts ...; 'depends on the national transposition'
proposedGenericDecision: The 'Member States' / 'national transposition' framing is EU-directive-specific and presupposes the institution sits inside an EU Member State whose transposition it must consult. This is acceptable WITHIN the EU-instrument sections, but the cautionary note should be reframed so the generic obligation ('consult your home jurisdiction's implementing law') is primary and the EU-Member-State case is the worked instance. Keep the EU detail but lead with the jurisdiction-neutral verification duty already present in sec:rm-beyond-eu.
rationale: A national-transposition assumption stated in EU-Member-State terms without acknowledging that a non-EU adopter has no NIS2 transposition at all. sec:rm-beyond-eu and the last itemize bullet partly mitigate this, but the cautionary note's default voice still assumes EU membership.

surfaceForm: Where this chapter cites the GDPR, NIS2 or the AI Act, a non-EU institution substitutes its host jurisdiction's functional analogue
proposedGenericDecision: This paragraph is the mitigation mechanism and is already role-based ('host jurisdiction's functional analogue'). The only residual specificity is the asymmetry (EU = default, non-EU = the one who substitutes). Decision: retain the substitution mechanism but, if the chapter is reframed per the chapter-wide row, present GDPR/NIS2/AI-Act themselves as one host-jurisdiction analogue among the parameterised set rather than the baseline.
rationale: Already a role-based substitution clause and the principal de-specification lever; flagged to note that its effectiveness depends on whether the chapter-wide EU-default framing is also generalised. The named analogues (UK GDPR, LGPD, CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA) are explicitly illustrative, so they are not blockers.

surfaceForm: 'this Reference' / 'the architecture and the playbook of this Reference' (recurring)
proposedGenericDecision: 'This Reference' is the suite's self-designation, not institution-specific. No action for institution-agnosticism; recorded only to confirm it does not embed a UL document title.
rationale: Self-referential to the document suite, jurisdiction- and institution-neutral. Not a specificity blocker; logged as explicitly cleared.
